newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares nudge index to ninth straight high.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares nudge index to ninth straight high.

text.p: Egypt share prices nudged the all-share index to another record high on Wednesday, with Amriyah Cement leading turnover in the market.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index closed at 324.83 points, up 0.05 points on 324.78 points at Monday's close. Volume was 85.22 million pounds ($25.06 million).
The market was closed on Tuesday.

About 26.58 million pounds worth of Amriyah shares changed hands, and the share price edged up 0.34 pounds closing at 71.85. The Egyptian state last week said it completed the sale of 3.4 million shares in Amriyah, reducing its stake to about 48 percent.

The second most active share was one of the two big privatised real estate companies, Heliopolis Housing and Development. Its prices as well as those of Medinet Nasr Housing and Development eased this week.

"In the market in general a lot of profit-taking is taking place in two of the major players in the market, Heliopolis and Medinet Nasr. But we feel they will rebound again," said broker Sherif Cararah, of EFG/Hermes.

About 15 million pounds of Heliopolis shares changed hands. It closed a pound higher at 547. Medinet Nasr was also in the top ten in terms of turnover but its share fell 17.01 pounds to close at 419.99.

Turnover in Commercial International Bank (CIB) shares almost doubled to 11.32 million pounds compared to Monday, as expectations of a 10-for-one share split continued, brokers said. Its share price closed unchanged at 600 pounds.
The CMAindex for openly traded firms fell to 510.39 from 511.01 points on Monday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 222.55 from 222.32.
Out of 76 shares traded, 32 advanced, 16 declined and the other 28 ended the day unchanged.
